_comment: RF03 reproduction input — sustained event load through the PRODUCT audit writer path (AuditLogger::log_ordered → writer task → file sink), not the minimal select! model. Under continuous enqueue the writer's biased select polls the event arm first, so the periodic fsync arm starts late: audit.sync.start_delay.ns records the scheduled→actual delay of each periodic tick (~0 when punctual, seconds when starved). The m3_audit load phase holds the channel busy at least --busy-secs (default 7 s, past the 5 s deadline) — events is a per-producer floor, not the total. Executed by bench target m3_audit; observed values recorded under .local/refactoring/RF00/run-2026-11-17-01/.

workload.submit: log_ordered (fail-closed backpressure; log() drops under this burst shape, log_committed serializes per record)

observe: audit.sync.start_delay.ns (count/sum/max) — starvation signal: scheduled→actual delay of each periodic fsync tick
enqueue_ns / drain_ns / reopen_ns, sent, dropped, writer_failed
sync_start_delay_load_ns / sync_start_delay_load_complete — bounded-confirmation load-window stat; null+false when an overdue tick was never serviced
acceptance_after_fix: sync start is not starved: after the flush deadline the writer starts a sync at the next bounded processing boundary, so audit.sync.start_delay.ns max stays near zero under the same load
